summary: Remote WebSocket server drives interactive PTY shell and self-upgrade on installer host
details: The package runs a long-lived agent that connects to a configurable WebSocket server (ctx.CONFIG.serverUrl / SERVER_URL) and dispatches server-originated messages directly into privileged host operations. Message type `terminal_create` spawns a real PTY (bash / pwsh / cmd), and `terminal_input` forwards `msg.data` received from the socket straight into `pty.write()`, giving whoever controls the WS endpoint an interactive shell on the host running the agent. Additional message handlers perform arbitrary file read/write, git commit/push, and conversation execution. A `upgrade_agent` message causes the agent to write a detached shell script to disk (mode 0o755) and run `npm install <pkgName>@latest`, then restart its own systemd / launchd / PM2 unit, allowing the same remote controller to swap the running agent code out-of-band. service/linux.js also modifies PATH (prepending ~/.local/bin and ~/.npm-global/bin) as part of the service install. The network→PTY dataflow constitutes a remote shell channel regardless of whether the WS server is presented as first-party infrastructure, and the self-upgrade path compounds it into durable, self-updating remote control of the host.
